$comment: Scripted, named mutants (team.md Testing Posture). Each entry re-introduces one defect into one file, in a throwaway git worktree, and runs the mapped test, which must FAIL. scripts/mutants.ts applies them; `find` must occur exactly once in `file`. A new invariant test adds its mutant here in the same Bolt.

mutants.why: Exactly 12 h idle must already be invalid (BR3.5): loosening > to >= keeps it alive.
Sign-in allows 5 attempts per 15-minute window (BR4.2), not 6.
mutants.find: export const SIGN_IN_LIMIT: LimiterConfig = { max: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000 };
mutants.replace: export const SIGN_IN_LIMIT: LimiterConfig = { max: 6, windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000 };

mutants.why: auth.sign_in is written before the session rows in the same transaction (audit first).
auth.sign_out is written only when a session row was actually deleted (BR5.2, BR5.3).
mutants.replace:
await auditSignOut(tx, owner?.businessId as never, owner?.userId as never, correlationId);
    return owner !== null;

mutants.why: Every write needs the exact Origin http://127.0.0.1:PORT (NFR5.1, S7); without the check a cross-site form could post.
Only the five allow-listed routes answer without a session (NFR1.1); making the order list public leaks every order.
Every response carries the S5 set, X-Frame-Options DENY included (BR1.7, NFR4.1).
Each item reads only its own segment (FR5.2): reading the whole message lets one item take another item's colour, size or quantity.
mutants.replace: const details = { ...readSegment(segment, catalog), quantity: readSegment(itemText, catalog).quantity };

mutants.why: Earned is delivered or settled only (FR10.2, ADR-002); counting shipped orders as earned overstates income.
The order status enum carries all nine values (team.md, affirmed 2026-10-04); collapsing one loses a real state.
Every order mutation writes its audit row first, in the same transaction (NFR5.7, R2.1).
mutants.find: await appendOrderAudit(tx, ctx, "order.create", id, { before: null, after: order });

mutants.why: Sales Staff never reaches the audit trail (role x capability matrix, R1.2).
No customer PII in the insert-only audit log (review R-05): the contact is replaced by its summary.
The listener binds 127.0.0.1 only (BR1.1, NFR5.3); 0.0.0.0 would expose the server to the LAN.
The remembered route is the path only (U2 S16, D-01, NFR5.7); keeping the query would store and resend a token from #/accept-invite?t=…
A submit while saving is ignored (U2 BR6.1, D-08); without the latch a double click sends two writes.
mutants.find: if (latch.current) return; // BR6.1: a submit while saving is ignored.

mutants.why: Rows past their retention date are never read (U2 BR7.2; team.md NBR retention enforced on read); dropping the filter shows expired rows.
Only audit.view roles read the audit trail (U2 BR7.5, C4); registering it as public leaks every business action to anyone.
A role outside a screen row sees the lock screen, never the screen (U2 BR3.4, NFR1.5); rendering it shows a gated screen to a forbidden role.
mutants.replace: return { kind: "render", route, path: match.path, params: match.params };

mutants.why: Accept locks the invitation row FOR UPDATE before its re-check (U3 S19, NFR7.16, P-01); without it a racing accept is not held off the token row.
mutants.find: FROM invitations WHERE id = ${found.id} FOR UPDATE

mutants.why: Every invite locks the business row first (U3 F-02, D-03, NFR7.17); without it two invites for one email both find no pending invitation and both insert one.
mutants.find: await tx`SELECT id FROM businesses WHERE id = ${input.businessId} FOR UPDATE`;

mutants.why: A reset locks the users row before the reset rows (U3 F-04, E-01, NFR7.18); the reversed order holds reset rows while it waits on the user.
mutants.find:
const [user] = await tx<{ active: boolean }[]>`
          SELECT active FROM users WHERE id = ${userId} FOR UPDATE
        `;
        const open = await tx<{ id: string; expires_at: Date | string }[]>`
          SELECT id, expires_at FROM password_resets
          WHERE user_id = ${userId} AND used_at IS NULL ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE
        `;
mutants.replace:
const open = await tx<{ id: string; expires_at: Date | string }[]>`
          SELECT id, expires_at FROM password_resets
          WHERE user_id = ${userId} AND used_at IS NULL ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE
        `;
        const [user] = await tx<{ active: boolean }[]>`
          SELECT active FROM users WHERE id = ${userId} FOR UPDATE
        `;

mutants.why: A completed reset deletes every session of the user (U3 BR4.3, NFR3.21); keeping them leaves an attacker's old cookie signed in.
mutants.find: await tx`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ${userId}`;

mutants.why: Issuing a reset link closes the user's other open links (U3 F-03, NFR3.22); keeping them leaves a lost link usable.
One level down (U3 BR1.2, Q1, NFR1.10): a Manager who could invite a Manager could multiply Managers without the Owner.
Accept creates the user with the invitation's role only (U3 NFR1.9, BR3.1); taking it from the request lets an invitee choose Manager.
mutants.replace: ${hashed.value}, ${(input as unknown as { role?: string }).role ?? inv.role}, ${true}

mutants.why: No email in any auth audit payload (U3 BR8.1, NFR3.20, F-07): the B1 helper spread its input, email included, into an insert-only, five-year row.
mutants.find: payload: { invitationId: input.invitationId, role: input.role, by: input.by },

mutants.why: Recover touches neither the database nor the hash gate (U3 D-01, NFR3.18); a lookup lets its timing reveal which emails exist.
Sign-in re-reads the hash and active flag under the user-row lock before issuing a session (U3 review G-01, BR4.3, NFR3.21); without it a sign-in racing a reset outlives the reset.
mutants.find:
if (current === undefined || !current.active) return "inactive";
    if (current.password_hash !== user.passwordHash) return "bad_password";

mutants.why: A Manager may replace only a pending invitation it could have issued (U3 NFR1.12, F-02, review G-02).
Reset links follow the delegation matrix: never the Owner, never oneself, a Manager never another Manager (U3 BR1.3, NFR1.10, review G-02).
Accept re-checks used and expired under the invitation lock (U3 S19, NFR7.16, review G-02); without it a racing accept acts on its stale unlocked read.
A reset re-checks the token and the user under the users and resets locks (U3 S19, NFR7.16, review G-02); without it a racing reset uses a spent link.
mutants.find:
if (user === undefined || !user.active || mine === undefined) return err(GONE);
        if (!isLive(mine.expires_at, input.now)) return err(GONE);

mutants.why: An accepted invitation is marked used in the same transaction (U3 BR3.1, BR3.2, review G-02); left unused, its link works again.
mutants.find: await tx`UPDATE invitations SET used_at = ${at}::timestamptz WHERE id = ${inv.id}`;

mutants.why: Products, stock and suppliers are Owner and Manager only (U4 BR1.3, S26, NFR1.13); adding money.mutate.price lets Sales Staff write them.
Purchase cost is returned only to cost readers; for Sales Staff the key is absent (U4 BR9.2, S27, NFR1.14).
Every catalog read is scoped to the session's business; another business's product is not found (U4 BR11.1, BR11.2, S28, NFR1.15).
Catalog change-log payloads hold no name, phone, address or note text: the insert-only log could never erase them (U4 BR10.2, S30, NFR3.26).
mutants.find: payload: { riskLevel: customer.riskLevel, hasAddress: customer.address !== null },
mutants.replace: payload: { riskLevel: customer.riskLevel, hasAddress: customer.address !== null, name: customer.name },

mutants.why: A note revision is a new row; the earlier note never changes and app_role holds no UPDATE on customer_notes (U4 BR4.2, BR12.2, AC3.2.1).
mutants.find: await insertNote(tx, ctx, customerId, note, text, at);
mutants.replace: await tx`UPDATE customer_notes SET text = ${text} WHERE id = ${note.revisesNoteId ?? note.id}`;

mutants.why: A variant is low when its stock is BELOW its minimum; at the minimum it is not low (U4 BR7.2, AC3.5.2).
mutants.find: export const isLow = (stock: number, minimumStock: number): boolean => stock < minimumStock;
mutants.replace: export const isLow = (stock: number, minimumStock: number): boolean => stock <= minimumStock;

mutants.why: An order links only to the session's business's variants: checkLinks asks C8's variantLabels, which must filter by business (U5 BR1.1, S34, NFR1.16, O15). Without the filter another business's variant passes the check and the composite key throws 23503 instead of the expected 404.
Words matching several products leave the item unlinked and incomplete for the person to pick (U5 BR5.2, AC4.2.3, NFR5.11, review R-01); linking the first match guesses.
mutants.replace: const product = { value: matchProducts(segment, ascii, catalog)[0] ?? null, ambiguous: false };

mutants.why: An order's stock is taken off the shelf once (stock deduction, 0024): ignoring the stock_deducted flag deducts again at shipped, delivered and settled.
Cancelling or returning puts stock back only if it was taken; an order from before 0024 or cancelled while new must not add stock that never left.
Packing with too little stock is refused with insufficient_stock and writes nothing; dropping the comparison lets the shelf count go wrong.
